title: You Think Uniforms Turned Stanford Guards Cruel, Yet Archive Tapes Proved Coaching
description:
Clinical Case Briefing — Philip Zimbardo, Craig Haney & Curtis Banks (1971): The Stanford Prison Simulation & Modern Archival Critique, grounded in Craig Haney, Curtis Banks, Philip Zimbardo (1972) (Stanford University Psychology Building Basement (Jordan Hall), Palo Alto, California). Empirical findings show that in August 1971 at Stanford University, Craig Haney, Curtis Banks, and Philip Zimbardo recruited male college students via a $15-per-day newspaper ad and screened 75 applicants down to 24 psychologically healthy finalists.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: A coin flip assigned 12 men as 'Guards' (given khaki uniforms, whistles, and silver mirrored sunglasses hiding eye contact) and 12 as 'Prisoners' (given numbered smocks, stocking caps, and ankle chains in a converted basement hallway of Jordan Hall).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Craig Haney, Curtis Banks, Philip Zimbardo (1972). Interpersonal Dynamics in a Simulated Prison. https://doi.org/10.21236/ad0751041
- Veronika Káplová (2026). Philip Zimbardo, Daniel Hartwig. Philip Zimbardo: Paměti psychologa. E-psychologie. https://doi.org/10.29364/epsy.551
- Fatma Yaşın, Sezin Başbuğ (2016). Prof. Dr. Philip Zimbardo ile Kötülük Psikolojisi Üzerine. Nesne Psikoloji Dergisi. https://doi.org/10.7816/nesne-04-07-07
